input.rationale: Thirteenth turn: CheckRun 4e8ef1701c7b4020a40640d1a7f2e4e2 (completed, exit_code 0) evaluates all five comparisons of the follow-up basis completely - the stale-decided case is violated again at witness index 9, and the four decision-formation comparisons hold (batched vector equality and index/content consistency at index 1, leader-change prefix preservation at index 3, recovery convergence at index 4). The two open decision-formation questions now receive accounts built on that receipt instead of remaining empty.

interpretations.rationale: Current account, scoped to the exercised configuration: with batch_size 4 and eight entries proposed on the leader and eight on a follower, the batched accept path kept the reported decided vector and its index-to-content mapping consistent - when every node reported decided_idx 16, the receipt event at index 1 records all_logs_equal true, index_content_consistent true (each node's entry readable at index i equals the element it reports for index i) and all_values_present true over exactly the sixteen proposed values. The suspicion that a follower's batched append would report an accepted index not corresponding to the entries it holds is therefore not supported in this schedule. This is a question-level account built from another investigation's fixed experiment (the batched case runs in experiment 39f7d4c4c0484f7e94edbc51cbd78c2b, whose declared investigation is the recovery question), so no defect judgment is claimed and the conclusion is recorded as explained rather than bound to this question's own experiment.
counterevidence: The check is a proxy: it verifies agreement of the decoded decided vectors and of the entry readable at each index, not the internal accepted-index number a follower puts into its Accepted reply, which is not exposed by the public API.

All 16 proposals were emitted before the cluster was pumped, so the case does not cover a follower receiving a batched AcceptDecide while the leader's decided_idx already exceeds the follower's accepted idx during the same exchange; the earlier local probe that did cover that path also agreed, but it is not a retained receipt.
Nothing in the case exercises compaction, so the index/content comparison is only valid while no prefix has been trimmed or snapshotted.
limitations: One deterministic schedule of one configuration (three nodes, majority quorum, batch_size 4, no reconfiguration, no message loss).
Only the dev profile was exercised, as in every run of this session.
interpretations.joint_history: Cited receipt 4e8ef1701c7b4020a40640d1a7f2e4e2 comes from experiment 39f7d4c4c0484f7e94edbc51cbd78c2b, whose declared investigation is the recovery/compaction question b2606c6f3c1148c5af396ef701166e6f-question-0; the batched and leader-change cases were added to that harness as further cases of the same execution. Compatibility for this question's account: same captured snapshot 02fcea099fe34a70931e7ba3878d0d47, same package and harness target, same feature set and dev profile, no target files modified, and the cited events (index 1) are emitted by the batched case running inside that single execution, so they are observations of the same fixed inputs the receipt records. No other receipt contributes to this account.

interpretations.rationale: Current account, scoped to what was measured: after a six-entry prefix is decided, removing the leader and electing a replacement among the survivors leaves the decided prefix unchanged on every surviving node (receipt event index 3, prefix_preserved true, all_logs_equal true, decided_everywhere true at decided_len 10), and rebuilding the removed leader from its persisted storage converges to the same decided vector as the survivors without altering the prefix (event index 4, recovered_caught_up true, recovered_prefix_preserved true, recovered_all_logs_equal true). So on the exercised leader-change and recovery path, LogSync/AcceptSync did not truncate or reorder decided entries. The account is conditional because the question also asks about the specific adoption branch where a promise reports a newer accepted round or a longer accepted log than the leader's: that branch is the one the stale-decided case exercises (follower handle_prepare taking the create_log_sync path from the preparing leader's decided index), and there the response aborts rather than adopting, which bounds but does not answer the general question for configurations where that request stays inside the responder's compacted prefix.
counterevidence: The measured case has the replacement leader elected among nodes that already agreed on the prefix, so the replacement's log was not shorter than the survivors' decided prefix; a leader with a genuinely shorter log adopting through a promise is not covered by these two comparisons.
No message loss, reordering or duplicate delivery is applied in this case, so the sequence-number and re-prepare repair paths are not exercised.
Neither case includes compaction, so the snapshot/delta branch of the log update is not exercised here.
limitations: One deterministic schedule of one configuration (three nodes, majority quorum, batch_size 2).

The adoption branch that the question names is only partially covered, through the failing compaction interaction recorded under b2606c6f3c1148c5af396ef701166e6f-question-0; no run in this session observed that branch completing outside the contrast case's snapshot-enabled configuration.
interpretations.joint_history: Both cited events come from the same receipt 4e8ef1701c7b4020a40640d1a7f2e4e2 and the same execution of experiment 39f7d4c4c0484f7e94edbc51cbd78c2b, whose declared investigation is the recovery/compaction question; they are the leader-change case's result and its recovered-leader result, produced by that one test run. Compatibility: same captured snapshot, package, harness target, feature set and dev profile, with no target files modified; events 3 and 4 are the pre- and post-recovery observations of the same case, so they share one history rather than two independent runs.

interpretations.rationale: Source-only reading settles the premise the question asked about: `InternalStorage` maintains `accepted_idx` as a log LENGTH (`AppendEntries`/`AppendSync` semantics: `state_cache.accepted_idx = sync.sync_idx + sync.suffix.len()`, increment by one per appended entry and by one for a StopSign), `LeaderState.accepted_indexes` is seeded with 0 for every pid and written with that same length (`set_accepted_idx`) or with a follower-reported length (`handle_accepted` -> `set_accepted_idx(from, accepted.accepted_idx)`), `is_chosen(idx)` counts entries with `accepted_indexes[k] >= idx`, and the leader passes the reported length (`accepted.accepted_idx`) as well as its own length. `get_min_all_accepted_idx` (used by `trim(None)`) takes the minimum of the same lengths. So the decide step, the trim step and the reported values agree on length semantics; no off-by-one between them is visible in the captured code.
counterevidence: The name `accepted_idx` reads like an entry index, and `read_decided_suffix`/`read` use indices; any future consumer that mixes the two conventions would be off by one, but no such consumer is present in the captured code paths I read.
limitations: This is a source-only account; it establishes the units used by the captured code, not that every message producer/consumer pair is consistent at runtime, which the experiment in this update does not yet cover.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading identifies a concrete gap: the follower-side log-update construction can request a suffix at an index below the requestor's own compacted index, and the in-memory storage implementation turns that request into an arithmetic panic (dev profile) rather than the empty suffix its trait requires. A non-retained local run (draft/tmp/ws/omnipaxos/tests/probe4.rs) reproduces exactly that: with v_stale = (accepted 6, decided 3, round r1), f_healthy = (accepted 6, decided 6, compacted 6) and the old leader crashed, f becomes the accepted leader; when v calls try_become_leader, f's Prepare handling panics with 'attempt to subtract with overflow' at omnipaxos_storage/src/memory_storage.rs:103 while computing its log update, and v's preconditions (decided 3 < f's compacted 6, accepted 6 at the trim bound) are unchanged by that panic. Because that execution is local construction feedback and not a retained receipt, this account claims only a conditional expectation, not an asserted defect.
counterevidence: The panic is raised by `MemoryStorage` (a dependency crate in the same captured snapshot) while the core's call is legal per the `Storage::get_suffix` contract, so responsibility is split between the core's choice of prefix and the storage implementation's unchecked subtraction; a fix in either location would remove the observed failure.

Upstream's trim bound (`get_min_all_accepted_idx`) is what keeps other sync paths away from the compaction boundary, so this path needs the phase where the follower's accepted round is newer than the preparing leader's while the preparing leader's decided index is older than the trim point; a scenario without a crash-recovered node holding a stale decided index does not reach it.
limitations: The local reproduction is not a retained receipt; the next action repeats the same prefix as a fixed-input experiment in the omnipaxos package and cites its CheckRun.
The release-profile consequence (empty suffix instead of a panic, leaving `sync_log` to set accepted_idx 3 with decided_idx 6) is a source-level inference in this update and was not measured.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: in the captured snapshot, a follower handling a Prepare builds its log update from the preparing leader's decided index whenever that leader's accepted round is older, and for a non-snapshot Entry type it does so through get_suffix(common_prefix_idx) without comparing that index to its own compacted index. The retained run reaches exactly that state and shows the failure: three nodes decide three entries, all three accept three more while one node is kept below decided 3 (accepted_idx 6, decided_idx 3), the leader trims to 6 (legal: every node accepted 6) so the healthy follower's compacted_idx becomes 6 while the stale node misses the forwarded Compaction::Trim, the leader is then removed and the healthy follower becomes the accepted leader under ballot n=2, and the stale node's try_become_leader makes it prepare with decided_idx 3 / accepted_idx 6. CheckRun 18e0d44919ed4eb786f1231efbab552c parses six events; the admission alias takeover_ready matches event 3 (healthy_follower_is_leader true, healthy_follower_compacted_idx 6, stale_node_decided_idx 3, stale_node_accepted_idx 6), and the result event 4 records outcome 'aborted_panic' with panic_message 'attempt to subtract with overflow' at omnipaxos_storage/src/memory_storage.rs:103 while healthy_follower_compacted_idx is still 6. The declared predicate 'outcome == completed' is therefore contradicted by a complete witness with correlated prerequisites. Responsibility in this snapshot is shared and both parts are captured code: the core chooses the below-compaction prefix (legal under the Storage trait, which specifies returning an empty vector when entries do not exist for the interval, so the request itself is permitted) and MemoryStorage::get_suffix violates that contract by computing from - trimmed_idx unchecked, aborting the node. The observable consequence for the cluster is availability loss on a legal recovery/compaction/election sequence: the surviving healthy follower dies while handling an ordinary Prepare, and the takeover cannot be evaluated.

knowledge.assertion: with snapshots disabled the log update is built as get_suffix(common_prefix_idx) with no comparison against the responder's own compacted index
MemoryStorage::get_suffix(from) subtracts trimmed_idx unchecked and panics with overflow checks enabled for from < trimmed_idx

counterevidence: The aborting arithmetic is in the captured MemoryStorage implementation, not in the core crate: the core's call is legal per the Storage::get_suffix contract, so this witness proves the captured snapshot fails this path, not that the core's prefix choice is itself a contract violation.

Scoping: for a snapshot-capable Entry type the same Prepare takes the snapshot branch (decided_idx 6 > common_prefix_idx 3) and the suffix is then read at the responder's own decided index, so the failure observed here is specific to entries without snapshots (or to decided_idx <= common_prefix_idx); the run does not show a snapshot-capable variant failing.

The stale state is produced by dropping whole messages of one kind addressed to one node (decisions while it must stay at decided 3, then AcceptSync after it must promise without accepting); that is ordinary message loss under the target's fault model, and the state it produces (accepted 6 / decided 3 / older accepted round with the durable log intact) is what a crash-recovered node legitimately holds, but the drops are part of the harness's construction rather than of a natural crash alone.
limitations: Only the dev profile was measured (overflow checks enabled, as in the controller's cargo test invocation); the consequence when overflow checks are off is not observed, so no claim is made here about a silently wrong log update in that configuration.
The captured memory storage backend was used; whether the persistent storage backend also reaches a failing endpoint for the same request, and which endpoint, was not measured.

The witness is a single deterministic schedule of one cluster size (three nodes, majority quorum, batch_size 3, NoSnapshot entries, trim index 6); the account is scoped to that exercised configuration.

The panic aborts handling before any reply is produced, so the run witnesses the abort itself; the further cluster-level consequences (a stalled or inconsistent log) are not measured by this execution.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: a node whose decided index lags its accepted index (crash-recovered before the later decisions reached it, having accepted far enough for every peer to pass the trim bound) can prepare against a peer that has already compacted past that decided index. The peer then builds its log update from the preparing node's decided index - 3, below its own compacted index 6 - and for an Entry type without snapshots that request goes to the storage as get_suffix(3) with no comparison against the peer's compacted index. Measured outcome: the peer aborts. In the cluster run (CheckRun 18e0d44919ed4eb786f1231efbab552c, event 4) the abort was 'attempt to subtract with overflow' raised inside MemoryStorage::get_suffix while the responder still held accepted 6 / decided 6 / compacted 6 and the preparing node reported decided 3 / accepted 6. The contrast run (CheckRun 5ffdf2f10d3943d39f56133f08c42a6e) reproduces that with witness index 2 and, holding every input equal apart from the Entry type, shows the same request completing when snapshots are enabled (comparison 1 holds at index 5), because then the snapshot branch runs and the suffix is read at the responder's own decided index. The persistent backend case is also violated (witness index 8): there the storage returns an error instead of the empty suffix its trait specifies, and the abort is raised by the core crate itself at create_log_sync's expect(READ_ERROR_MSG) (omnipaxos/src/sequence_paxos/mod.rs:428, message 'Error reading from storage.: ErrHelper'), so the failure is not an artifact of the in-memory backend. Consequence bound by these runs: on a legal crash-recovery plus compaction plus election sequence, a healthy replica that must answer an ordinary Prepare is destroyed instead of producing log support, which removes the participant needed to restore eligible participation; the defect is asserted for entries without snapshots (or any configuration where the selected branch reads a suffix below the responder's compacted index) and is not claimed for the snapshot-enabled in-memory combination, which completed.

a6e1fe52471c4864a0b3042da04de8e0-gap-0.explanation: Both halves are now measured in CheckRun 5ffdf2f10d3943d39f56133f08c42a6e: a snapshot-capable Entry type does not reach the failing request on this path (comparison 1 holds at event index 5, outcome 'completed' with compacted_idx 6), while the captured persistent RocksDB backend does fail for the request that the in-memory backend fails on (comparison 2 violated at event index 8, outcome 'aborted_panic', panic_message 'Error reading from storage.: ErrHelper'). The persistent variant aborts at a different site: its get_suffix returns an error rather than the empty vector the Storage trait specifies, and the core's expect in create_log_sync raises the abort, so the defect is not specific to MemoryStorage.

The contrast experiment 8fa16297ae994c0c8f9127fd2c6af430 (CheckRun 5ffdf2f10d3943d39f56133f08c42a6e) delivers the same prefix messages directly to a single responder in the same state and reproduces the same abort for the same non-snapshot case (index 2) while adding the snapshot-enabled (holds) and persistent-backend (violated, different abort site) cases. The two receipts are compatible: neither modifies target sources, both use the captured crate's public API, and the contrast case that answers the gap is the one whose construction the cluster receipt independently reached through real traffic; the earlier receipt remains the evidence that the state arises naturally, while the contrast receipt is the basis for the bounding claims.

interpretations.rationale: Current account, scoped to the exercised configuration: with batch_size 4 and eight entries proposed on the leader and eight on a follower, the batched accept path kept the reported decided vector and its index-to-content mapping consistent - when every node reported decided_idx 16, the receipt event at index 1 records all_logs_equal true, index_content_consistent true (each node's entry readable at index i equals the element it reports for index i) and all_values_present true over exactly the sixteen proposed values. The suspicion that a follower's batched append would report an accepted index not corresponding to the entries it holds is therefore not supported in this schedule. This is a question-level account built from another investigation's fixed experiment (the batched case runs in experiment 39f7d4c4c0484f7e94edbc51cbd78c2b, whose declared investigation is the recovery question), so no defect judgment is claimed and the conclusion is recorded as explained rather than bound to this question's own experiment.
counterevidence: The check is a proxy: it verifies agreement of the decoded decided vectors and of the entry readable at each index, not the internal accepted-index number a follower puts into its Accepted reply, which is not exposed by the public API.

All 16 proposals were emitted before the cluster was pumped, so the case does not cover a follower receiving a batched AcceptDecide while the leader's decided_idx already exceeds the follower's accepted idx during the same exchange; the earlier local probe that did cover that path also agreed, but it is not a retained receipt.
Nothing in the case exercises compaction, so the index/content comparison is only valid while no prefix has been trimmed or snapshotted.
limitations: One deterministic schedule of one configuration (three nodes, majority quorum, batch_size 4, no reconfiguration, no message loss).
Only the dev profile was exercised, as in every run of this session.
interpretations.joint_history: Cited receipt 4e8ef1701c7b4020a40640d1a7f2e4e2 comes from experiment 39f7d4c4c0484f7e94edbc51cbd78c2b, whose declared investigation is the recovery/compaction question b2606c6f3c1148c5af396ef701166e6f-question-0; the batched and leader-change cases were added to that harness as further cases of the same execution. Compatibility for this question's account: same captured snapshot 02fcea099fe34a70931e7ba3878d0d47, same package and harness target, same feature set and dev profile, no target files modified, and the cited events (index 1) are emitted by the batched case running inside that single execution, so they are observations of the same fixed inputs the receipt records. No other receipt contributes to this account.

interpretations.rationale: Current account, scoped to what was measured: after a six-entry prefix is decided, removing the leader and electing a replacement among the survivors leaves the decided prefix unchanged on every surviving node (receipt event index 3, prefix_preserved true, all_logs_equal true, decided_everywhere true at decided_len 10), and rebuilding the removed leader from its persisted storage converges to the same decided vector as the survivors without altering the prefix (event index 4, recovered_caught_up true, recovered_prefix_preserved true, recovered_all_logs_equal true). So on the exercised leader-change and recovery path, LogSync/AcceptSync did not truncate or reorder decided entries. The account is conditional because the question also asks about the specific adoption branch where a promise reports a newer accepted round or a longer accepted log than the leader's: that branch is the one the stale-decided case exercises (follower handle_prepare taking the create_log_sync path from the preparing leader's decided index), and there the response aborts rather than adopting, which bounds but does not answer the general question for configurations where that request stays inside the responder's compacted prefix.
counterevidence: The measured case has the replacement leader elected among nodes that already agreed on the prefix, so the replacement's log was not shorter than the survivors' decided prefix; a leader with a genuinely shorter log adopting through a promise is not covered by these two comparisons.
No message loss, reordering or duplicate delivery is applied in this case, so the sequence-number and re-prepare repair paths are not exercised.
Neither case includes compaction, so the snapshot/delta branch of the log update is not exercised here.
limitations: One deterministic schedule of one configuration (three nodes, majority quorum, batch_size 2).

The adoption branch that the question names is only partially covered, through the failing compaction interaction recorded under b2606c6f3c1148c5af396ef701166e6f-question-0; no run in this session observed that branch completing outside the contrast case's snapshot-enabled configuration.
